title: The Morning Brief: Trade deadline reshuffles, Infantino's isolation deepens, Kuwaki claims maiden major
dek: The MLB trade deadline moved contenders to reinforce their rotations and rosters on Sunday, while FIFA's governance crisis hardened into formal institutional opposition as England joined Wales and UEFA in withdrawing support for Gianni Infantino. In golf, Shiho Kuwaki won her first major at the Women's Open after Esther Henseleit's drive struck a marshal in sudden death.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Three sports produced watershed moments on August 3: baseball's deadline catalyzed deadline trades for contenders chasing playoff spots; FIFA's political ground shifted when a second major confederation formally abandoned Infantino ahead of his March 2027 re-election; and golf crowned a new major champion in circumstances outside the runner-up's control.
bottom_line: August 3 produced reshuffled rosters on baseball's final deadline day, formal institutional rejection of Gianni Infantino across multiple confederations, and a new major champion crowned by circumstance beyond the runner-up's control. The Cubs and Guardians bet on late-summer additions to reach October; the Sparks bet on retreat and rebuilding; the English FA's withdrawal joins UEFA's legal threat in narrowing Infantino's March 2027 path to re-election; and Kuwaki inherits a major title while Henseleit's near-miss remains defined by a marshal's placement. Watch the coming weeks for whether other confederations follow England's lead, whether the Guardians' new depth sustains through the playoffs, and whether Infantino issues a response to the coordinated institutional opposition.
body: The MLB trade deadline, set for Monday at 6 p.m. ET, triggered a Sunday sprint of roster moves as contenders with playoff ambitions locked in their rotation and bench depth. The Cleveland Guardians made two separate moves: acquiring All-Star left-hander Foster Griffin from the Washington Nationals to bolster their postseason rotation, then trading catching prospect Jacob Cozart to the Los Angeles Angels for outfielder Jo Adell, a 27-year-old with full team control through 2027. Adell posted a strong 2025 season (.778 OPS, 37 home runs, 98 RBIs) but has slumped to .239/.287/.395 in 2026; the Guardians are betting a change of scenery in a contending clubhouse reignites last year's form. The Chicago Cubs, sitting 6.5 games behind the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Central, acquired 35-year-old right-hander Kevin Gausman from the Toronto Blue Jays in exchange for Triple-A outfielder Brett Bateman and Class-A infielder Ty Southisene. Gausman carries postseason pedigree, a 3.83 ERA in 14 career playoff games, but has stumbled recently with a 6.47 ERA over his last eight starts, a concern as the Cubs press toward October.

In women's professional basketball, the Los Angeles Sparks formally retreated from contention by trading five-time All-Star Kelsey Plum to the Phoenix Mercury for forward Monique Akoa Makani, a 2027 first-round pick, and a 2028 second-round pick. Plum is averaging 23.9 points and 6.4 assists through 12 games, both career highs, and leads the WNBA in scoring. The trade signals the Sparks' abandonment of their window after recent veteran acquisitions failed to stabilize the club. Meanwhile, in the Minnesota Lynx's 108-100 victory over the Indiana Fever, Olivia Miles scored 28 points but drew her third technical foul of the season, triggering a WNBA fine under the league's accumulated technical foul rules.

FIFA's governance crisis deepened as the English Football Association moved to formally withdraw its support for president Gianni Infantino, joining Wales as the second major confederation to publicly abandon him ahead of his March 2027 re-election bid. Infantino needs 106 votes from FIFA's 211 member nations to secure a fourth and final term. UEFA has gone further, sending Infantino a document preservation letter and raising the possibility of legal action over his now-scrapped proposal to create a $20 billion private entity to run the World Cup. UEFA's 55 member nations voted Thursday to boycott FIFA competitions in protest. The sequence marks a formal institutional escalation: from public criticism to withdrawal of prior support to legal threat. The honest read on the sourcing is that England's withdrawal crystallizes European opposition into a documented roster, but whether African and Asian confederations follow remains unconfirmed in the reporting.

In golf, Shiho Kuwaki won the 2026 Women's Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes, finishing at five under par and defeating Esther Henseleit in a sudden-death playoff. Both players finished regulation tied; Henseleit forced the playoff with a dramatic 45-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole in regulation. On the second playoff hole, Henseleit's drive struck a course marshal and was redirected into a gorse bush, ending her bid to become only the second German woman to win a major championship. Kuwaki advances from tour professional to major champion; Henseleit's loss hinges on an element beyond her control.

In women's soccer, Marc Skinner departed as head coach of Manchester United Women by mutual consent after five years in charge, exiting with one year remaining on his contract. Skinner oversaw the club's first major trophy, an FA Cup win in 2024, but also their lowest-ever league finish, a fifth-place WSL standing that same season. In college football, Notre Dame and USC agreed to resume their rivalry with a four-game series beginning in 2030, with Week 1 matchups in Los Angeles (2030) and South Bend (2031). The Week 1 scheduling compromise resolves a years-long stalemate created when USC joined the Big Ten. Alex Eala, 21, won her first WTA title at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington, defeating Jessica Pegula 4-6, 6-4, 6-0 to become the first Filipina to win a WTA 500 event. Eala avenged a prior loss to Pegula at the 2025 Miami Open semifinal. In cricket, the ICC Anti-Corruption Tribunal banned Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy, a 26-year-old United States international, for eight years after finding him guilty of match-fixing, encouraging another participant in match-fixing, and obstructing the investigation during the Abu Dhabi T10 League in 2025.
